text: Beyond the mortal veil, the very air belongs to death, and every speeding arrow riding on it will always find its target.
Through the centuries, as Arkhan laboured alongside Nagash, he learned that this work, also, begins with servitude, a sacramental ritual unto itself.
Nagash brings death none can make peace with – not an impersonal force, but an expression of absolute will. For mortals, no peace is possible, but neither is victory.
Undead beasts upend all laws of nature. Nature’s purpose is to thrive. Undead beasts sow death and  desolation. Yet even they have a master.
Spoken of in fear and awe in histories long turned to dust, the great ones among the Undead have bowed under the only name that matters.
Chariot wheels hailed a Nehekharan ruler's arrival, and that of certain victory. It has never been more certain now when they serve Nagash.
Nehekharans, in their worship, were the first to stamp spirit upon stone. Nagash's triumph over the inanimate is far greater.
Death was once a point of no return. Every passage beyond the veil is a gust of Shyish blowing one way – until Nagash decreed that it should blow the other.
No living being would dare fly in a winged beast’s claws, for fear of a dire drop to the bottom. For Nagash, a deathly drop is inevitable, for there is no bottom.
A Necromancer's morbid infatuation with death finds its fullest form in Dieter Helsnicht. The power pales to the depths of such devotion.
Nagash's will is the eye of a storm. The storm itself is these warriors’ blades. In its wake, souls swirl in Shyish, still unaware of their death.
Spirits trapped in confusion,wandering lost, sunken to the depths and buried under stone are bent to their purpose by a greater darkness.
After they reap, there will be no further sowing. The world will be a cold cairn, the tomb-silent, its roads forever haunted.
A  warrior's pride is misused by a petty ruler’s frail claim to power. Nagash has excised such failings. Service to greatness is what remains.
A  warrior's pride is misused by a petty ruler’s frail claim to power. Nagash has excised such failings. Service to greatness is what remains.
As the seas dry up and the fraught lives of those who sailed them begin their course in unlife's element, their devastation shall know no bounds.
The steeds have shed every living excess from their frame so their riders can deliver death in the excess demanded by their master.
Where Nagash walks, the legions follow. They swell not just at his behest, but at the mere trace of his mark upon the land, growing by the moment.
A legacy of barrow-mounds and faded crests, and memories of an unstoppable advance awaken anew as steeds are mounted for the last time.
Krell has ever walked the path of bloodshed and despair. His master's goal may be to end all despair, but first the world will have its share in Krell.
Everything dies. Malignant daemonic essences, mortal memory, arcane paths to ascension - all try to defy it. Yet none changes the essence of this truth: Nagash.
In the depths sinks the flotsam of body and soul. The tides of peace and struggle come and go, but the deep waits eternal, as does Nagash.
The purest light is that of oblivion. In the light, one is nowhere. It blinds the eye and empties the mind, making it a twin of darkness, and both are one in Nagash.
Nehekhara's power arose out of worship. Even the great kneel to something greater. The road to divinity never ends. Yet through Nagash, it will.
What we almost see – but not fully – we fear. All souls dwell in shadow and fear that it will swallow them. The shadow of all shadows is Nagash.
Across the point of no return, a world awaits that is the darkest mirror of existence, a void that will eat away at the core of every being, save one. Nagash.
Blood courses through flesh and time, but some find ways to steal it to make their flesh timeless. What they stole, Nagash always possessed.
No one can plumb the depths of Luthor Harkon's mind, for it is an abyss, blind and unfathomable. His shattered self is half-undone. The rest belongs to Nagash.
A soul’s silent memory and a skull’s gaping stillness are every mortal’s fate. Yet it is time souls wailed and  bones screamed once last time.
Bearers of the writ and wealth of a kingdom which cannot be beggared and whose ruler cannot be opposed.
In the dark of night, Mannfred's mind excelled at scholarship and lowly cunning, and his thirst for power grew to rival his thirst for blood.
The Hammurai descended in mortal struggle and always triumphed, except once. Now ghastly reflections of their past selves, they are no lesser.
None of his Nagash's past failures were such. They were steps along his way to become what he is now, and the path to his pinnacle and the end of all else is at its conclusion.
An immortal spirit unshackled, and possesed of raw power, it vowed its service to reclaim its name and its shattered mind - a boon yet to be bestowed.
Secretive even as Lahmia’s Queen, Neferata eventually found refuge in that secrecy. Yet Nagash sees all, for she was ever his unwitting, if precocious, student.
Forests of long-hafted weapons shall rear up from the hollow earth and there remain after the end, still as trees, the air black with iron.
Those who gather for Nagash are marching to the end of all history, clarions silent, banners tattered – dire symbols of Nagash’s will.
Every speck of dust in Nagash’s domain is imbued with his touch, every edifice or ruins is under his eye. The sky itself is bounded by his shadow.
Nagash's hordes sprout into existence from the dust he leaves behind, and to the dust they will return, but not before they heap yet more of it upon the world.
A gigantic construct of war's shape on the horizon makes mockery of hope. They lay waste to all illusions of permanence, for such illusions must end.
The mortal purpose which these bones is now dust. The living core is gone. Shyish is their marrow now, and purpose is much greater.
Blades and arrows cannot fight death. A shield bearing the marks of service to Nagash is a constant reminder of how foolish such beliefs are.
Nagash’s Nehekharan kin claimed immortal glory, and were still claimed by death, which they revered. Death and worship they shall have eternally, in Nagash.
The shadow of Nagash bids dread colossi out of their element, to challenge his presence. They die and are enchained, nothing but fleeting shadows in his eye.
Sea-faring vampires have wasted their immortality in aimless wandering, seeking "freedom" like mortal children. Their course is now charted forever on.
Before they served, they sought to rule like mortals. Lowly ambitions and acting out parts of an inferior life are unnecessary. Nagash’s glory needs no performance.
Though not his creation, Vampires have inherited Nagash's utter arrogance. They still seek to show themselves the first and most superior among Nagash's servants.
A being of unassailable force, Vlad’s monstrous shadows of human passion and obsession have inured him against fear, even from Nagash. Even so, he shall serve.
None can stay Walach Harkon's charge towards glory. But no Vampire can outrun their thirst. Some claim his sire Abhorash could. Walach simply does not want to.
No wizard can truly bend the Winds to their will though some well know their nature. But Nagash’s way has ever been to impose his nature over all he touches.
The ghoulish and grave-rotted, the living that do not live, the dead who do not stay so – all of them Nagash’s instruments to pry the world open and for him to sup on its marrow.
